name: lotr
summary: LOTR, one gateway to rule them all: a fixed four-tool MCP surface in front of any number of downstream connections, with a registry of who talks to whom, as whom, from which machine

settings.summary: LOTR agents: separate reader and writer agents (split), or one read/write agent per task (combined).
settings.detail:
split     readers (jira, m365, github, runner) hold find + call_read only; writers hold
          find + call_write (+ call_consent); a change is composed from your words alone  (default)
combined  one agent, gt-lotr:gateway, holds all four gateway tools: fewer hops, cheaper

The split is what stops text inside a read result (an issue body, an email) from steering a
write, an injection. combined removes that protection, so it only takes effect while the
lockdown level is insecure; at any other level it is ignored, the effective mode stays split,
and the reason is stated. Irreversible operations (send mail, merge, delete) still go through
the consent step (call_consent, your Touch ID or Windows Hello) in either mode.

settings.summary: A generated MCP agent's result up to this many tokens (characters / 4) comes back as it is; a larger one is summarised.
settings.detail:
The size, in estimated tokens (characters / 4), up to which the call script of an agent made by
`lotr onboard` returns a result to the conversation whole. A larger result is stored whole in a private
file and a summary comes back instead. Lower it to keep more out of the conversation; raise it if the
summaries lose what you need. One connection can differ: lotr onboard tune CONNECTION --direct-tokens N.

settings.summary: Summarise large results of a generated MCP agent with a no-tools model (on), or show a short preview instead (off).
settings.detail:
on   a large result is summarised by a headless model that has no tools, so only the summary reaches
     the conversation; the full result is kept in a private file
off  a large result gets a short preview and the file path, with no model call
If the summariser cannot run, the preview is used and the reason is printed.

settings.summary: The model that summarises a large result of a generated MCP agent (haiku, the cheapest, by default).
settings.detail:
The summariser has no tools and sees only the result text. haiku is cheapest and was enough for a
26,000-character JSON result in the phase 36 check (one sample); try sonnet if a summary loses what you need.
